q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: In the last 7 days (2026-10-07..2026-10-13), several Meta campaigns spent meaningful ad budget but recorded zero attributed orders (orders with touchpoints = 0) — they are likely wasting money and should be checked or paused. Top examples by spend (order-attribution basis: Orders with touchpoints):

- DOG SHOES-10OCT-CS — Spend: ₹6,714 · Orders: 0  
- DOG BEDS-12OCT-CS — Spend: ₹5,135 · Orders: 0  
- TH-103-K9HARNESS-10OCT-CS — Spend: ₹5,037 · Orders: 0  
- TH-348-FUSIONHARNESS-03OCT — Spend: ₹4,867 · Orders: 0  
- TH-073-SMARTSIP-11OCT — Spend: ₹4,050 · Orders: 0  
- TH-229-BLUEJAY SNEAKS-10TH-OCT — Spend: ₹3,604 · Orders: 0  
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-12OCT — Spend: ₹3,269 · Orders: 0

Why this matters (ordered by impact): 
- These campaigns together represent several thousand rupees of spend with no attributable purchases in the week — direct wasted ad budget.  
- Some similar-name campaigns in the same list did produce orders (e.g. TH-383 variants, TH-279), so the issue looks campaign-specific (creative, targeting or delivery), not product-level.  
- Attribution used: Orders with touchpoints (ad touchpoints → order); this is order-date attribution, not the Finance P&L view.  
- Data note: queries cover last 7 complete days and are current as of 2026-10-14; ad platform / attribution data are hourly and should be mostly fresh.

Worth checking: pause or reduce budget on the listed campaigns, then run a quick drilldown by ad set / creative and landing-page LPVs to confirm whether low clicks/LPVs or poor post-click conversion is the cause.
